subject: general
question: Who is the author of the Booker Prize-winning novel "Midnight's Children"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Salman Rushdie**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Salman Rushdie** is the author of the world-renowned novel **Midnight's Children**, which was published in **1981**. The book is a celebrated work of **magical realism** and **post-colonial literature**. ***Hence, Option 2 is correct.***

• The novel was awarded the prestigious **Booker Prize** in **1981**. Its literary significance was further cemented when it won the **Booker of Bookers** in **1993** (to mark the **25th anniversary** of the prize) and the **Best of the Booker** in **2008** (to mark the **40th anniversary**).

• **Vikram Seth** is a famous Indian novelist and poet, best known for his epic novel **A Suitable Boy**, published in **1993**. Although he is a major figure in **Indian English literature**, he did not write Midnight's Children. ***Hence, Option 1 is incorrect.***

• **Jhumpa Lahiri** is an **American** author of Indian descent. She is widely known for her debut short story collection, **Interpreter of Maladies** (**1999**), which won the **Pulitzer Prize for Fiction** in **2000**. Her famous novels include **The Namesake** and **The Lowland**. ***Hence, Option 3 is incorrect.***

• **Amitav Ghosh** is a distinguished Indian writer known for works such as **The Shadow Lines**, **The Glass Palace**, and the **Ibis Trilogy**. In **2018**, he became the first author writing in **English** to be honored with the **Jnanpith Award**, India's highest literary prize. ***Hence, Option 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Salman Rushdie**: Born on **June 19, 1947**, in **Bombay** (now **Mumbai**), **India**, just weeks before the country gained independence. His writing often deals with the **Indian subcontinent** and the **diaspora**. He was **knighted** by **Queen Elizabeth II** in **2007** for his services to literature.

• **Midnight's Children Plot**: The story is narrated by **Saleem Sinai**, who is born at the exact stroke of midnight on **August 15, 1947**. His life is telepathically linked to **1,001** other children born in the first hour of **India's independence**, all of whom possess **supernatural powers**.

• **Historical Context**: The novel serves as an allegory for the history of **modern India**, covering major events such as the **Partition of India**, the **1971 war** that led to the creation of **Bangladesh**, and the **Emergency** (**1975-1977**) imposed by **Indira Gandhi**.

• **Literary Style**: Rushdie utilizes **magical realism**, a style where **mythical** or **fantastical** elements are woven into a **realistic** setting. This allows him to explore complex themes of **national identity**, **memory**, and **cultural hybridity**.

• **Other Works by Rushdie**: His other notable books include **Shame** (**1983**), **The Satanic Verses** (**1988**), **The Moor's Last Sigh** (**1995**), **Quichotte** (**2019**), and **Victory City** (**2023**).

**Important Points__**

• **The Booker Prize**: Established in **1969**, it is one of the most prestigious literary awards in the world, given annually for the best **novel** written in **English** and published in the **United Kingdom** or **Ireland**.

• **Indian Winners of the Booker Prize**: Apart from **Salman Rushdie**, other Indian or Indian-origin authors who have won the prize include **V.S. Naipaul** (**1971**) for 'In a Free State', **Arundhati Roy** (**1997**) for 'The God of Small Things', **Kiran Desai** (**2006**) for 'The Inheritance of Loss', and **Aravind Adiga** (**2008**) for 'The White Tiger'.

• **Geetanjali Shree**: In **2022**, she became the first Indian author to win the **International Booker Prize** for her novel **Tomb of Sand** (originally 'Ret Samadhi'), which was translated from **Hindi** by **Daisy Rockwell**.
